family_verdict: Right, but only partly. Most of what the five instructions actually name is pure orthographic fingerprint -- typos, homophones, paragraph spacing, typographic conventions -- which a spellchecker or one proofing pass supplies without improving anything about the story. But the shared parent (the text was revised, or written by someone practised at revising) also produces changes that are constitutive of quality rather than symptomatic of help: continuity that holds, planted details that pay off, prose with nothing left to cut. That is what phrases like stable naming and controlled diction in R3B02 are half-reaching for. So the MIXED flag is justified: a genuinely quality-relevant component is tangled in, and the family should be decomposed and retired rather than dual-reported.
